reading.title: The cost of fast fashion
reading.text: For the third consecutive year, global clothing production has broken records. Cheap fashion has clear benefits for shoppers, but its consequences for the environment are serious. The textile industry uses huge amounts of water, and most clothes are thrown away within a year. In 2013, a factory collapse in Bangladesh killed more than 1,100 workers; subsequent investigations found that warning signs had been ignored. Several managers were prosecuted. Campaigners say the sequence is always the same: a disaster, a promise to change, and then business as usual.

items.s: Clothing production has reached a record level for three years in a row.
Most clothes are kept for more than a year.
All the managers responsible for the collapse went to prison.
Campaigners believe the industry rarely changes after disasters.

qs: Who is responsible for the consequences of fast fashion: companies or consumers?

write: Many people buy cheap clothes and throw them away quickly. Why is this happening? What effects does it have on the environment?
